source.title: An Analysis of Optimizer Choice on Energy Efficiency and Performance in Neural Network Training

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. It contains some apparent layout or extraction artifacts, but the relevant performance table is readable.
record.tranche_reason: The paper compares optimizers and reports validation accuracy on image-classification datasets, bearing on V4. It does not measure the training-to-test gap directly.
record.gate_note: The reported validation accuracies bear on optimizer-related held-out performance. Training accuracy and train-to-validation gaps are not reported, so these results cannot establish whether performance differences persist at equal training performance. Energy, duration, emissions, memory, and ranking results do not measure the claim versions and are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study compares held-out image-classification accuracy across adaptive optimizers and momentum SGD, directly bearing on V4. V4 does not require a measured generalization gap: equal or better training performance is an optional qualification. Fixed optimizer configurations and early stopping limit the comparison's scope.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors emphasize dataset-dependent performance and environmental trade-offs, similar accuracy on MNIST, SGD's highest accuracy on CIFAR-100, and AdamW's balance of accuracy and environmental efficiency. Their attribution to dataset complexity is an interpretation, rather than an independently isolated causal result.
record.recipe_differences: The paper uses CNNs on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and CIFAR-100, with fixed optimizer configurations and early stopping; it reports validation accuracy but not training accuracy or generalization gaps.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset changes the reported optimizer accuracy pattern.
record.problems: The study reports validation accuracy but no training accuracy, so it does not measure the generalization gap. Hyperparameters are fixed rather than dataset-optimizer-specific optimized, and the authors note the experiments use only small image-classification models on Apple M1 Pro hardware.
record.rows_left_out: No result rows were extracted because the reported accuracy values do not measure the train-to-test gap named by V4, and no other version's target measure is tested. Table I reports validation accuracy means and standard deviations by dataset and optimizer.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting compared with natural-label and random-label held-out accuracy.
Width increases beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and the contribution of local connectivity.

Training performance; language benchmarks; systematic learning-rate and schedule tuning; broader tuning; controlled tests of decoupled weight decay or switching from Adam to SGD. Including AdamW alone does not establish recovery through decoupled weight decay.
Batch-size comparisons with fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its correlation with generalization gaps.
Accuracy effects of removing memorized versus random examples.

missing.what: Restore the omitted validation-accuracy comparisons as V4 rows, including means and standard deviations for all eight optimizers on each dataset. Momentum-SGD baselines are 0.9784 ± 0.0044 on MNIST, 0.6216 ± 0.0680 on CIFAR-10 and 0.2061 ± 0.0493 on CIFAR-100. Although rows_left_out declares these omissions, its rationale incorrectly requires a generalization-gap measure. Record the 15 seeds, fixed optimizer-specific hyperparameters, 80/20 split, patience-five early stopping and 50-epoch maximum.
missing.locator: Table I; Sections III.A.2, III.D–E; Algorithm 1

record.verdict_notes: There are no existing rows to fix. The study is not an original source. Fixed literature-based configurations, differing weight decay, variable stopping epochs and unreported training performance prevent attributing held-out differences specifically to generalization at equal training fit. They do not invalidate the held-out comparisons as evidence on V4. Standard deviations are reported, but statistical significance of optimizer accuracy differences is not.

Removing memorized training examples and measuring test-accuracy effects.

relationships.condition: MNIST; fixed optimizer configurations and early stopping
relationships.reason: Table I and the discussion describe similar accuracy across optimizers: momentum SGD reaches 97.84%, while adaptive methods range from 97.83% to 98.29%. This setting shows little meaningful adaptive-optimizer penalty. Based on text; no rows were extracted.
relationships.display_finding: Reported accuracy was similar across optimizers, but this comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10; Adadelta, Adagrad and RMSprop versus momentum SGD
relationships.reason: Table I reports validation accuracy of 53.57%, 51.65% and 56.07%, respectively, below SGD's 62.16% under the fixed configurations. Based on text; no rows were extracted.
relationships.display_finding: Reported validation accuracies for Adadelta, Adagrad, and RMSprop trail momentum SGD, but these comparisons remain unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-10; Adam, Adamax and NAdam versus momentum SGD
relationships.reason: Table I reports higher mean validation accuracy for Adam (65.13%), Adamax (66.53%) and NAdam (63.85%) than SGD (62.16%). These reverse the proposed disadvantage in this setting; significance is not reported. Based on text; no rows were extracted.
relationships.display_finding: Adam, Adamax and NAdam reportedly achieved higher mean validation accuracy than momentum SGD, but the comparisons remain unverified and significance was unreported.

relationships.reason: Table I reports nearly equal validation accuracy: AdamW 62.67% versus SGD 62.16%, with standard deviations of 4.64 and 6.80 percentage points. There is no clear adaptive-method disadvantage here. Based on text; no rows were extracted.
relationships.display_finding: Reported AdamW and momentum SGD validation accuracies were close relative to their variation, but this comparison remains unverified.

relationships.condition: CIFAR-100; all seven adaptive optimizers versus momentum SGD
relationships.reason: Table I reports SGD validation accuracy of 20.61%, exceeding every adaptive optimizer's mean of 3.36–9.89% under fixed configurations and early stopping. Based on text; no rows were extracted.
relationships.display_finding: Reported momentum SGD validation accuracy exceeds every tested adaptive optimizer under fixed configurations and early stopping, but the comparisons remain unverified.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
